newsitem.title: INDIA: Stocks close up at India's National bourse.
newsitem.headline: Stocks close up at India's National bourse.

text.p: ** (1015 GMT) - Pivotals finish higher at National Stock
Exchange (NSE), undertone weak
** Bombay Stock Exchange (BSE) closed for festival holiday,
opens on Sunday briefly for auspicious "moorat" session
to herald the Hindu New Year
** Normal BSE trading resumes only next Wednesday after
holidays
** Blue-chips gain on short-covering by operators
** NSE 50-stock index up 9.93 points or 1.13 pct to 884.93
Share prices ended in positive territory at the National Stock Exchange (NSE) on Friday, helped by short-covering in blue-chips," traders said.
They said short-covering by speculators in pivotals ahead of a long market closure led to a rise in share prices.
"It was a holiday mood today --not much action in the market," said dealer Rakesh Chandak at brokerage Lloyds Finance.
The 50-stock National stock finished 9.93 points or 1.13 percent higher at 884.93, off 885.65.
Shares of ITC rose 6.95 rupees to close at 256.55 in volumes of 6.47 million shares.
Traders said backwardation charges in ITC at the Bombay Stock Exchange (BSE) at close of weekly account on Thursday indicated heavy short-sold positions in the stock.
"ITC is likely to be the star performer on Monday, with short-covering pushing up the prices," said dealer Sanjeev Choithani at brokers Pashupati Advani.
Backwardation costs imply over-sold positions.
A federal agency on Friday arrested the deputy chairman of ITC Ltd and a senior executive of the company in connection with alleged foreign exchange violations involving $100 million.
Two former chairmen of ITC Ltd, K.L. Chugh and J.N. Sapru, were arrested last week and remanded to judicial custody until November 13 by a local court.
SBI rose 4.30 rupees to 218.20, Reliance 1.80 to 187.50, TISCO 0.35 to 168.75, BSES 5.40 to 193.40, L&T 4.05 to 224.0 and ACC 15.25 to 1,433.25.
The NSE is open on Monday.
-- ANSHUMAN DAGA, Bombay newsroom +91-22-265 9000
